While GPU demand remains robust, Nvidia has begun worrying about where customers will get the money to buy its chips. On August 10, Nvidia announced it would join forces with six major Wall Street financial institutions to establish a series of independent computing power financing platforms, with plans to gradually mobilize more than $500 billion in third-party capital. The collaboration targets the funding bottleneck in the GPU sales chain—if customers cannot borrow money, even surging computing demand will struggle to translate into actual orders. But why now? How will this financing machine work? And if computing power revenue falls short of debt obligations and GPU residual values come in below expectations, who ultimately bears the risk?

01 Five-year contracts underpin GPU loans, but short-term customers are shut out

To understand why Nvidia is bringing Wall Street into the GPU ecosystem, one must first revisit the AI credit market before this initiative. According to SemiAnalysis estimates, AI-related debt balances will exceed $7 trillion by 2029, second only to the U.S. residential mortgage financing market at roughly $13 trillion. Behind this massive debt demand lies the ever-expanding capital expenditure of AI infrastructure. SemiAnalysis projects that annual AI capital expenditure (Capex) will far exceed $2 trillion by 2028; cumulative capex from 2024 to 2029 will reach approximately $11.1 trillion. These expenditures include AI IT such as GPUs, supporting CPUs, networking, and storage, as well as the data centers that house them.

For a decade, major internet companies have tried to boost worker efficiency. Online documents, WeCom, clock-ins and approvals— tools kept changing, seemingly transforming office workflows, yet the time actually freed up never seemed to shrink. Look at the elevator ads around you: on one side is WorkBuddy, on the other Doubao and Qianwen. Even airport lounges are saturated with AI office scenarios. items.raw_excerpt: 荣耀上一次让全行业意外，是 2020 年从华为独立出来。 但这一次，是一部手机。 几天前，荣耀 CEO 李健在广州正式发布 Robot Phone，9.59 毫米厚的机身里，塞着一个四自由度的钛合金机械云台，能够实现跟随音乐律动、拟人化交互、自动追焦等功能，产品定价 9999 元起。据李健在发布会上透露，算上前期新品预约，荣耀 RobotPhone 预定量已超 40 万台。 对行业而言，Robot Phone 是一个全新“物种”，在手机行业仍在追寻系统全面 AI 化的时期，荣耀凭借着在具身智能领域的技术积累，成功将两个看似相隔甚远的行业“捏”到了一起。 荣耀这一落子也恰逢其时。回过头看，2023 年是各家对模型大脑的比拼，而到了 2025 年，故事早已经向着“这具大脑能住进什么样的身体”发展，在这一概念热度空前的当下，荣耀也收获了一大波流量。 如今复杂的市场局面下，摆在荣耀面前的 Robot Phone 既是可选项，但也是必选项。 在一众友商中，小米汽车业务打开了新的增长曲线；CyberOne 人形机器人展示了小米在具身智能领域的布局。vivo 成立机器人 LAB 独立中心，专注消费级机器人研发。OPPO 也在端侧 AI 和智能体上持续投入。 摆在荣耀面前的选项不多，Robot Phone 刚好是一条最契合的路。某种角度看，荣耀更像手机行业的“理想汽车”，想用具身智能打开一个比手机更长的叙事，同时是一家手机公司给自己找的一张新身份牌。 手机团队走进具身赛场 2025 年 3 月，李健在 MWC 巴塞罗那发布“阿尔法战略”，而这也成了荣耀这一年多在具身领域动作的开始。 彼时，李健宣布荣耀将从“智能手机制造商”升级为“全球领先的 AI 终端生态公司”，未来五年投入超过 100 亿美元，全球研发人员占比达到 70%，AI 专利超过 2100 项。 动作随之而来，荣耀把 AI 相关

Recently, Tang Kai, President of OPPO's Software Engineering Business Unit, attended the Alipay AI Ecosystem Partner Conference. At the conference, Tang Kai stated that a structural contradiction in the current development of Agents is that model capabilities have outpaced the organizational capabilities of the industry chain. "Today, building a To C Agent product with a good experience based on models is no longer difficult, but forming a real business closed loop is not easy." Tang Kai said that Agents need to better understand users, complete more real tasks, and call on rich services and tools to provide users with a better experience. However, the industry still has a large number of isolated services and ecosystem islands.  

Tang Kai, President of OPPO's Software Engineering Business Unit — Agent Industry Collaboration: A Global Catch-Up for AI  

At the end of 2024, Anthropic launched MCP, attempting to solve the connection problem between AI applications and external data and tools through open protocols. In 2025, Google launched the A2A protocol, providing a solution for Agents developed by different vendors and frameworks to communicate and collaborate with each other. By April 2026, A2A had gained support from more than 150 institutions and entered multiple mainstream cloud platforms.  

From "Agent connecting to tools" (MCP) to "Agent connecting to Agents" (A2A), the evolution of industry infrastructure points to the same question: as models become smarter, how to integrate fragmented demands, services, and industrial capabilities truly.
excerpt_i18n.es: Recientemente, Tang Kai, presidente de la división de ingeniería de software de OPPO, asistió a la Conferencia de Socios del Ecosistema de IA de Alipay. Durante el evento, Tang Kai señaló que una contradicción estructural en el desarrollo actual de los agentes es que la capacidad de los modelos ya ha superado la capacidad organizativa de la cadena industrial. «Hoy en día, no es difícil crear un producto de agente orientado al consumidor con una buena experiencia basada en modelos, pero no es fácil lograr un verdadero ciclo comercial cerrado», afirmó. Tang Kai añadió que los agentes deben comprender mejor a los usuarios, completar más tareas reales y requerir el acceso a servicios y herramientas abundantes para ofrecer una mejor experiencia. Sin embargo, en la industria actual todavía existen numerosos servicios y ecosistemas aislados.
